forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.go_wrong: Possible outcomes include dispelling effects, item depletion, damage, energy, or wrong destination.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.combines: Some results affect the user's items or magical effects.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.blocked_reason: The rule has multiple random failure outcomes, including damage and depletion.

forgotten-realms.rule.coin-metal-determi.name: Coin metal determines ordinary coin value
forgotten-realms.rule.coin-metal-determi.cost_or_limit: Coins are generally valued by their metal, except for locally supported tokens.

forgotten-realms.rule.coinage-conversion.name: Coinage conversion standard
forgotten-realms.rule.coinage-conversion.cost_or_limit: Ten copper pieces equal one silver, ten silver equal one gold, and ten gold equal one platinum.

forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-valuatio.name: Trade bar valuation
forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-valuatio.cost_or_limit: A one-pound silver bar is worth 5 gp and a one-pound gold bar 50 gp; heavier bars scale proportionally.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.name: Smokepowder and antimagic

effect.summary: Smokepowder does not function in antimagic fields or dead-magic areas.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.cost_or_limit: Restricted by antimagic or dead-magic zones.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.go_wrong: Its operation fails in those zones.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar lacks a field that disables an item’s operation.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.name: Smokepowder manufacture

effect.summary: Making smokepowder requires a specified feat and alchemical skill, and yields a fixed quantity.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.cost_or_limit: Craft Wondrous Item and Alchemy 9 ranks produce one pound worth 16 gp; one ounce fires a bullet.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.who_may: A creator meeting the stated prerequisites.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.blocked_reason: This rule concerns crafting prerequisites and consumable ammunition rather than a basic effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.name: Chultan material quality

effect.summary: Weapons made from inferior local materials take penalties to attacks and damage.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.cost_or_limit: A -2 penalty applies, with damage remaining at least 1.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.who_may: Characters using weapons made from inferior materials.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.combines: Materials include stone, wood, obsidian, or copper.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.blocked_reason: A numerical attack and damage modifier is directly usable.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.name: Chultan armor fatigue

effect.summary: Wearing sufficiently burdensome armor in the heat causes fatigue after an hour.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.cost_or_limit: Applies to armor with check penalty -5 or worse after one hour; fatigue lasts while worn and one further hour.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.go_wrong: Fatigue imposes -2 Strength and Dexterity and prevents running or charging.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.who_may: Characters wearing the specified armor in Chult.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.blocked_reason: The timed fatigue condition and penalties are directly representable.

forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.name: Purple Dragon’s fate and Cormyr

effect.summary: Some believe Cormyr will fall when the last Purple Dragon dies.

forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.cost_or_limit: The claim is presented as belief, not confirmed certainty.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.go_wrong: The kingdom may perish if the belief is true.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.who_may: Applies to Cormyr and the Purple Dragon.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.combines: The dragon’s death is linked to the kingdom’s fate.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.blocked_reason: A conditional world consequence can be represented as a rule.

effect.summary: An old agreement between the elves and the Dalesfolk.
A plot lead rather than a world mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.name: Deepingdale salmon restriction

effect.summary: Outsiders taking more than one salmon for a meal are treated as bandits.

forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.cost_or_limit: One salmon per outsider for a meal.
forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.go_wrong: Taking more brings a bandit accusation.

forgotten-realms.rule.four-dolphins-foun.name: Four Dolphins Fountain’s ward

effect.summary: Prevents scrying and eavesdropping magic from working in the courtyard.

forgotten-realms.rule.four-dolphins-foun.blocked_reason: The passage specifies a persistent area-wide magical suppression effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.name: Vauntagar creature cycle

effect.summary: Injured guarding monsters shift away and a fresh one takes their place.

forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.cost_or_limit: A cycle of monsters guards the pools
forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.blocked_reason: The rule requires extradimensional creature storage and replacement.

forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.name: Lake of Steam volcanic warming

effect.summary: Underwater volcanic activity keeps the bay warm and produces steam and mist.

forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.go_wrong: Cold nights obscure the waters with dense mist
forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.blocked_reason: The heat and mist can be represented with basic area effects.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.name: The Sisters’ welcome

effect.summary: Creatures of the Sisters allow deity-favored travelers to approach without challenge.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.cost_or_limit: Requires an invisible mark of nature-deity favor
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.go_wrong: Unfavored intruders may be warned of or opposed
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.blocked_reason: The mark-based access restriction can be represented as a conditional rule.

forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.name: Dire Wood's outer-ring containment

effect.summary: Aberrations within the Dire Wood cannot cross its outer ring.

forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.combines: Magical chaos emanates from the central butte
forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.blocked_reason: A persistent boundary preventing creatures from crossing needs an area-field mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.name: Fountains of Memory transport

effect.summary: A being entering a pool to return to a past time instead teleports to a random place.

forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.who_may: A being entering a pool to reach the past
forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.combines: The pools also reflect images of the past
forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.blocked_reason: Random relocation can be represented as a basic position-changing effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.name: The Memory of Steel

effect.summary: A magic weapon said to have lost powers in battle may regain them after immersion in a Fountain of Memory.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.cost_or_limit: Requires dipping the weapon into a Fountain of Memory
forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.who_may: A weapon owner able to reach a fountain
forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.blocked_reason: Restoring an item's lost powers requires a rule for powers embedded in items.

forgotten-realms.rule.stone-bridge-river.name: Stone Bridge river-binding

effect.summary: The bridge's magic holds the Dessarin River in place so it cannot change course.

forgotten-realms.rule.stone-bridge-river.cost_or_limit: The river remains fixed despite attempts to snake elsewhere
forgotten-realms.rule.stone-bridge-river.blocked_reason: Binding an entire river's course requires a persistent area-scale effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.chessenta-slave-fr.name: Chessenta slave freedom

effect.summary: A Chessentan slave-owner may free a slave at any time, sometimes rewarding exceptional work.

forgotten-realms.rule.chessenta-slave-fr.blocked_reason: A change in legal status is representable as a relation alteration.

forgotten-realms.rule.mulhorandi-temple-.name: Mulhorandi temple ownership of slaves

effect.summary: Mulhorand’s temples own the nation’s slaves and rent them to others.

forgotten-realms.rule.mulhorandi-temple-.cost_or_limit: Slaves are treated as temple property; harming one is treated as vandalism.
forgotten-realms.rule.mulhorandi-temple-.who_may: The temples own and rent slaves.
forgotten-realms.rule.mulhorandi-temple-.combines: A slave may rise to bureaucrat status with sufficient education.
forgotten-realms.rule.mulhorandi-temple-.blocked_reason: The rule concerns social relations and legal status.

forgotten-realms.rule.slaves-are-illegal.name: Slaves are illegal in Sembia

effect.summary: Slavery is officially prohibited, though estate-owning nobles flout the law.

forgotten-realms.rule.slaves-are-illegal.blocked_reason: This is a setting restriction that can be represented directly.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-rift-s-origin-.name: The Rift’s origin leaves no evidence of volcanic activity or raging watercourses

effect.summary: Whatever formed the Rift, ordinary volcanic or water erosion is not indicated.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-rift-s-origin-.combines: Contrasts with several competing supernatural origin accounts
forgotten-realms.rule.the-rift-s-origin-.blocked_reason: This setting fact requires no special game capability.

forgotten-realms.rule.luiren-s-games-all.name: Luiren’s Games allow magic in ridge running but forbid it in kite fighting

effect.summary: Ridge-running competitors may use and target magic; kite fighting is entirely magic-free.

forgotten-realms.rule.luiren-s-games-all.combines: Magic use in ridge running can expose a competitor to opposing magic
forgotten-realms.rule.luiren-s-games-all.blocked_reason: The rule can be applied directly in play.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-games.name: The Games

effect.summary: Luiren holds changing local, regional, and kingdomwide sporting events.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-games.combines: Includes ridge running and kite fighting
forgotten-realms.rule.the-games.blocked_reason: The passage provides enough setting detail for ordinary event play.

forgotten-realms.rule.veldorn-mutual-def.name: Veldorn mutual defense

effect.summary: Monstrous inhabitants promise to defend one another when attacked.

forgotten-realms.rule.veldorn-mutual-def.cost_or_limit: Applies when one of them is threatened.

forgotten-realms.rule.yuirwood-divinatio.name: Yuirwood divination concealment

effect.summary: Detection and scrying cannot reveal the forest; seekers see ordinary trees instead.

forgotten-realms.rule.yuirwood-divinatio.blocked_reason: This requires blocking divination and supplying a misleading visual result.

effect.summary: Some stone circles provide passage to other locations, including other worlds.
Control of particular underground places can shift quickly and violently.

forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.name: Bhaal water curse

effect.summary: Drinking the black water causes magical ill effects equivalent to a day-long curse.

forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.cost_or_limit: Applies to intelligent beings who drink the water.
forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.who_may: Intelligent beings who drink Bhaal water.
forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.where_from: River water tainted at Bhaal's death site.
forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.combines: Equivalent to enduring a curse spell for a day.

forgotten-realms.rule.changing-deities.name: Changing Deities

effect.summary: A divine caster abandoning a deity loses that deity's class features until requirements for the new faith are met.

forgotten-realms.rule.changing-deities.cost_or_limit: The caster must complete a quest for the new church and receive atonement from its representative.
forgotten-realms.rule.changing-deities.go_wrong: Features of the abandoned faith are lost during the transition.
forgotten-realms.rule.changing-deities.who_may: Clerics, druids, paladins, rangers who cast divine spells, and other divine casters.
forgotten-realms.rule.changing-deities.combines: After the conditions are met, the caster resumes applicable features under the new deity.

forgotten-realms.rule.pantheons.name: Pantheons

effect.summary: Foreign clerics keep their spells while traveling, but local powers may oppose proselytizing, temple-building, or holy war.

forgotten-realms.rule.pantheons.cost_or_limit: Nonhuman clergy avoid persecution by limiting those activities in human lands.
forgotten-realms.rule.pantheons.go_wrong: Foreign clergy may be driven off or assaulted if they recruit or establish a temple.
forgotten-realms.rule.pantheons.who_may: Clergy of foreign deities and local religious authorities.
forgotten-realms.rule.pantheons.combines: Spell access remains normal during travel.

forgotten-realms.rule.deity-power-rankin.name: Deity power ranking

effect.summary: A deity's rank indicates relative divine power, not changes to cleric abilities, spells, or most mortal affairs.

forgotten-realms.rule.deity-power-rankin.cost_or_limit: Ranks descend from greater deity to demigod.

forgotten-realms.rule.lolth-s-clerics-ar.name: Lolth’s clerics are always female

effect.summary: Only women can be clerics of Lolth.

forgotten-realms.rule.lolth-s-clerics-ar.blocked_reason: This restriction can be represented as a character-eligibility rule.

forgotten-realms.rule.mask-s-secret-tunn.name: Mask’s secret-tunnel temples

effect.summary: In large cities, Mask’s temples may connect to guilds by secret tunnels and serve as neutral meeting ground.

forgotten-realms.rule.mask-s-secret-tunn.blocked_reason: This is a world fact, not an unmodeled power effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shadow-weave.name: The Shadow Weave

effect.summary: A magical framework created by Shar and used by her sorcerer-monks.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shadow-weave.who_may: Shar’s elite sorcerer-monks use its power.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-shadow-weave.blocked_reason: A separate magical framework and its interaction with magic are not defined by the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.name: Final judgment prevents ordinary resurrection

effect.summary: After Kelemvor judges a soul, raising or resurrecting it requires a deity’s intervention, usually through miracle or wish.

forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.cost_or_limit: Divine intervention is required and likely entails negotiation with Kelemvor.
forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.who_may: A deity may intervene on the soul’s behalf.
forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.where_from: Kelemvor’s judgment in the City of Judgment.
forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.combines: The stated means include miracle or wish.
forgotten-realms.rule.final-judgment-pre.blocked_reason: The rule governs a dead soul’s availability for resurrection.

forgotten-realms.rule.faithless-are-boun.name: Faithless are bound into a dissolving wall

effect.summary: A supernatural mold holds the Faithless in the city wall and gradually dissolves their bodies, souls, and consciousness.

forgotten-realms.rule.faithless-are-boun.cost_or_limit: Applies to all souls judged Faithless.
forgotten-realms.rule.faithless-are-boun.go_wrong: The process ends in dissolution of the soul and consciousness.
forgotten-realms.rule.faithless-are-boun.combines: The supernatural mold prevents escape and breaks down the souls.
forgotten-realms.rule.faithless-are-boun.blocked_reason: It requires persistent postmortem soul transformation and destruction.

forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsiders-a.name: Native outsiders are not warded from their home plane

effect.summary: On their home planes, native creatures evade outsider-based warding that would prevent bodily contact or send them home.

forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsiders-a.cost_or_limit: Applies to creatures native to the plane they occupy.
forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsiders-a.combines: The passage cites protection from evil as an example.
forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsiders-a.blocked_reason: It specifies how a warding spell interacts with a creature’s home-plane status.

forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.name: Summoned outsiders come from alignment-appropriate planes

effect.summary: A summoned outsider comes from a plane or realm compatible with its alignment and type, often the caster’s current plane if suitable.

forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.cost_or_limit: Its source depends on alignment, type, and the plane’s or realm’s alignment.
forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.go_wrong: Some exceptions are noted, such as affinity between gnome deities and burrowing creatures.
forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.where_from: The planes and realms associated with Toril.
forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.combines: A deity’s alignment determines a realm’s alignment; shared planes reflect their resident powers.
forgotten-realms.rule.summoned-outsiders.blocked_reason: Choosing a creature’s source plane requires summoning rules beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.three-laws-of-the-.name: Three Laws of the Enclave

effect.summary: A local government must accept all three enclave laws before Thay establishes an enclave.

forgotten-realms.rule.three-laws-of-the-.go_wrong: Failure to protect lawful Thayan envoys may make the local government accountable to Thay.
forgotten-realms.rule.three-laws-of-the-.who_may: Applies to local governments and Thayan enclaves.
forgotten-realms.rule.three-laws-of-the-.combines: Comprises the Law of Sovereignty, Law of Trade, and Law of Crafting.
forgotten-realms.rule.three-laws-of-the-.blocked_reason: This is a political agreement and needs no effect beyond its stated conditions.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-soverei.name: The Law of Sovereignty

effect.summary: Treats the enclave as Thayan soil under Thayan law, while requiring Thayans to surrender a murderer who committed a crime outside it.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-soverei.cost_or_limit: Thayans patrol the enclave; slavery is permitted there, subject to the stated limits on local enforcement.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-soverei.who_may: Applies within a Thayan enclave and to its dealings with local authorities.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-soverei.combines: Local authorities may request surrender for crimes committed outside the enclave.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-soverei.blocked_reason: This rule defines jurisdiction and can be adjudicated directly.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-trade.name: The Law of Trade

effect.summary: Sets enclave prices below normal cost and allows slaves as payment under stated transport and local-law restrictions.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-trade.cost_or_limit: Goods and services are priced 10% below normal; certain free scrolls require an equal purchase of other magic items.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-trade.go_wrong: Local law may make slave sales or transport ineffective or unlawful.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-trade.combines: Includes the special exchange of zero-level scrolls and slave-payment provisions.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-trade.blocked_reason: The rule specifies prices and transaction conditions.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-craftin.name: The Law of Crafting

effect.summary: Restricts what enclaves make for sale and bars dangerous, crime-friendly, and high-value items.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-craftin.cost_or_limit: Typical production is limited to listed minor goods and items worth no more than 2,000 gp; items must bear required marks.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-craftin.go_wrong: The Thayans may be held responsible if an enclave-made item harms someone.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-craftin.combines: Enclaves may cast spells for hire; listed products include potions, scrolls up to fourth level, wands, and minor items.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-law-of-craftin.blocked_reason: The rule lists permitted and prohibited goods and their value limit.

forgotten-realms.rule.clone-slaying-comp.name: clone slaying-compulsion

effect.summary: Manshoon clones were compelled to kill rival versions of themselves; survivors later overcame this by spells or devices.

forgotten-realms.rule.clone-slaying-comp.cost_or_limit: Affects the clones; method of removal varies.
forgotten-realms.rule.clone-slaying-comp.combines: Some spells and devices can master the compulsion.
forgotten-realms.rule.clone-slaying-comp.blocked_reason: The mechanism forcibly controls a creature’s intent.

forgotten-realms.rule.manshoon-s-stasis-.name: Manshoon’s stasis clones

effect.summary: Manshoon had a dozen or more clones, each believing it was the original; their activation caused a struggle for survival.

forgotten-realms.rule.manshoon-s-stasis-.cost_or_limit: Only three clones remain in the account.
forgotten-realms.rule.manshoon-s-stasis-.mind: Each believed itself to be the real Manshoon.
forgotten-realms.rule.manshoon-s-stasis-.combines: Manshoon seeks voluntary consciousness transfer between clones.
forgotten-realms.rule.manshoon-s-stasis-.blocked_reason: Cloning, backup identity, and consciousness transfer are not represented by the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.thayan-enclave-pot.name: Thayan enclave potion pricing

effect.summary: Enclaves sell potions at a ten percent discount; making one from an eligible scroll costs the normal potion price.

forgotten-realms.rule.thayan-enclave-pot.cost_or_limit: Next-day commissioned work costs fifty percent extra; usual completion takes two to five days.
forgotten-realms.rule.thayan-enclave-pot.combines: Applies to potions and scrolls made to order.

effect.summary: Entering without using the gate or speaking with a guard is treated as an attack.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-a.name: Level Adjustment and Effective Character Level

effect.summary: Add level adjustment to character level to get ECL; use ECL to determine experience needed for advancement.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-a.cost_or_limit: Higher ECL delays class-level advancement; racial Hit Dice also count toward character capability.
forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-a.combines: Level adjustment and racial Hit Dice both contribute to effective power.

forgotten-realms.rule.racial-hit-dice-as.name: Racial Hit Dice as class levels

effect.summary: A creature with multiple Hit Dice functions as a multiclass character with levels in a racial class equal to its base Hit Dice.

forgotten-realms.rule.racial-hit-dice-as.cost_or_limit: The first racial Hit Die has maximum value for player characters.
forgotten-realms.rule.racial-hit-dice-as.who_may: player characters of creatures with multiple Hit Dice
forgotten-realms.rule.racial-hit-dice-as.combines: Racial Hit Dice and class levels contribute to ECL.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-e.name: Level adjustment experience cost

effect.summary: A character’s ECL determines the experience points needed to gain another class level.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-e.cost_or_limit: Characters with high level adjustment need more XP to advance.
forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-e.combines: Uses character level plus level adjustment.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-effective-level.name: +1 Effective Level

effect.summary: Gain class features and skill points for a class level, but not base attack, Hit Dice, hit points, or base saves.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-effective-level.cost_or_limit: Cannot raise a class above 20 or advance an abandoned class.
forgotten-realms.rule.1-effective-level.combines: Counts in the class-level listing as an effective class level.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-ability.name: +1 Ability

effect.summary: Add one point to an ability score.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-ability.cost_or_limit: Replaces the normal ability increase every four levels.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-attack.name: +1 Attack

effect.summary: Increase base attack bonus by one.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-attack.cost_or_limit: Does not grant an additional iterative attack.
forgotten-realms.rule.1-attack.combines: Monks also add it to unarmed attack bonus.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-bonus-spell-leve.name: +1 Bonus Spell Level

effect.summary: Gain one daily spell slot one level above the highest spell already cast in a class.

forgotten-realms.rule.1-bonus-spell-leve.cost_or_limit: Only available with 20 levels in a spellcasting class; slots can hold lower-level or metamagic spells.
forgotten-realms.rule.1-bonus-spell-leve.combines: Ability modifiers can add a bonus spell at the new level.

forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.name: Patron deity and return from death

effect.summary: A chosen patron allows ordinary return-from-death methods if the deceased is willing; an unclaimed soul can be reclaimed only before Kelemvor disposes of it, or later by miracle or wish.

forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.cost_or_limit: Unclaimed souls are disposed of after 1d10 days; after that, only miracle or wish restores life.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.who_may: Characters who died; the player may choose a patron at the moment of death.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.where_from: Faerûn; Kelemvor handles unclaimed souls on the Fugue Plane.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.combines: Raising, resurrection, or reincarnation can work before disposal.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-r.blocked_reason: It depends on the deceased soul’s status and a post-death deadline, which the basic effect grammar cannot represent.

forgotten-realms.rule.cardinal-rule-rega.name: Cardinal rule regarding characters and patron deities

effect.summary: A player should not be penalized for leaving a patron deity unspecified on the character sheet.

forgotten-realms.rule.cardinal-rule-rega.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward table rule, not an effect outside the basic grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.nonmagical-psionic.name: Nonmagical Psionics variant restriction

effect.summary: The campaign does not use the Nonmagical Psionics variant.

forgotten-realms.rule.nonmagical-psionic.cost_or_limit: The restriction applies to Faerûn campaigns using this guidance.
forgotten-realms.rule.nonmagical-psionic.who_may: Dungeon Masters and players using the variant.
forgotten-realms.rule.nonmagical-psionic.combines: Psionics Handbook rules may still be used.
forgotten-realms.rule.nonmagical-psionic.blocked_reason: It prohibits a category of rules variant rather than describing an effect the basic grammar can run.

forgotten-realms.rule.regional-feats-and.name: Regional feats and equipment for psionic classes

effect.summary: Psions and psychic warriors receive no regional feats or regional bonus equipment by default.

forgotten-realms.rule.regional-feats-and.cost_or_limit: The restriction may be relaxed if psionics has a larger role in the campaign.
forgotten-realms.rule.regional-feats-and.combines: Tashalar, Chult, Vilhon Reach, and Gray Dwarf regions may be treated as preferred regions if the restriction is relaxed.
forgotten-realms.rule.regional-feats-and.blocked_reason: This is a direct eligibility restriction rather than a game-world effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.time-controlled-ab.name: Time-controlled abilities

effect.summary: An ability with a weekly use limit becomes available again only after seven days have passed since its use.

forgotten-realms.rule.time-controlled-ab.cost_or_limit: Each use must wait seven days before it is available again.
forgotten-realms.rule.time-controlled-ab.combines: A campaign journal can track uses; tendays are an optional alternative with calendar complications.
forgotten-realms.rule.time-controlled-ab.blocked_reason: The rule can be run by tracking elapsed days.

forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.name: Invulnerability

effect.summary: When slain, a dracolich’s spirit returns to its phylactery and can seek a suitable corpse.

forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.cost_or_limit: A reptilian corpse must be within 90 feet for possession; without one, the spirit remains in its phylactery.
forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.go_wrong: Destroying the phylactery prevents future possession; a spirit without body or phylactery has an unknown fate.
forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.mind: The contained spirit cannot take actions other than attempting possession.
forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.combines: Requires a phylactery and a suitable corpse.
forgotten-realms.rule.invulnerability.blocked_reason: It specifies spirit persistence, a soul container, and transfer into a corpse.

forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.name: A spirit contained in a phylactery can sense suitable corpses

effect.summary: A contained dracolich spirit detects eligible nearby corpses and may attempt possession.

forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.cost_or_limit: The corpse must be reptilian or dragon and at least Medium-size within 90 feet; the original body is automatically accepted, while other attempts use Charisma checks.
forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.go_wrong: Failure against a particular corpse prevents any later attempt to possess that corpse.
forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.mind: The spirit cannot act except to possess a suitable corpse.
forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.who_may: A dracolich spirit held in its phylactery.
forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.combines: Successful possession animates the corpse; its form determines whether it becomes a dracolich or proto-dracolich.
forgotten-realms.rule.a-spirit-contained.blocked_reason: It defines post-death sensing, possession checks, and spirit transfer into corpses.

forgotten-realms.rule.resist-enchantment.name: Resist Enchantment

effect.summary: Rothé gain a +4 racial saving throw bonus against enchantment spells and effects.

forgotten-realms.rule.resist-enchantment.blocked_reason: The resistance is a simple defensive modifier.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-tearfall.name: The Tearfall

effect.summary: A catastrophe rearranged continents and seas and ended batrachi civilization.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-tearfall.where_from: A possible falling comet or ice moon

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-souls-and-th.name: Elven souls and the Tree of Souls

effect.summary: Ancient elves who remain on Toril may merge their souls into the Tree, increasing its power.

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-souls-and-th.cost_or_limit: Applies to ancient elves who choose to remain rather than pass to Arvandor
forgotten-realms.rule.elven-souls-and-th.blocked_reason: The rule defines a soul's after-death destination and fusion with a living vessel.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sundering-s-un.name: The Sundering's unintended Weave effects

effect.summary: Concentrating the Weave at Evermeet may have reduced its strength elsewhere, contributing to nodes, faerzress, and magic zones.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sundering-s-un.cost_or_limit: The proposed consequence is uncertain and not uniform across Toril
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sundering-s-un.go_wrong: Weave strength may be diminished beyond Evermeet
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sundering-s-un.combines: possible nodes, faerzress, dead magic zones, and wild magic zones
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sundering-s-un.blocked_reason: The rule describes persistent regional magical fields and zones, not a single-target effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.bukhara-spires-are.name: Bukhara Spires are permanent, two-way portals

effect.summary: none stated

forgotten-realms.rule.bukhara-spires-are.cost_or_limit: They allow passage in both directions and remain in place.
forgotten-realms.rule.bukhara-spires-are.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar lacks a mechanism for permanent interworld portals.

forgotten-realms.rule.silent-death-plagu.name: Silent Death plague

effect.summary: none stated

forgotten-realms.rule.silent-death-plagu.cost_or_limit: Killed fifteen to twenty percent of the population even in lightly affected areas, and was accompanied by crop blight and famine.
forgotten-realms.rule.silent-death-plagu.blocked_reason: The passage gives historical outcomes but no usable disease mechanics.

forgotten-realms.rule.imaskari-extradime.name: Imaskari extradimensional spaces

effect.summary: none stated

forgotten-realms.rule.imaskari-extradime.cost_or_limit: First permanent space created by artificers in –8123 DR.
forgotten-realms.rule.imaskari-extradime.blocked_reason: The passage names permanent extradimensional space, not represented by the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.orcgate-invasion.name: Orcgate invasion

effect.summary: Planar gates can bring armies and their deities from another world into Toril.

forgotten-realms.rule.orcgate-invasion.cost_or_limit: The passage does not state a gate's range or duration.
forgotten-realms.rule.orcgate-invasion.go_wrong: An opened gate can permit massive invasions.
forgotten-realms.rule.orcgate-invasion.who_may: Portal magic users can open such gates.

forgotten-realms.rule.wildtide-arrivals.name: wildtide arrivals

effect.summary: A wildtide portal can open again after an interval, allowing further migration from a distant sea.

forgotten-realms.rule.wildtide-arrivals.cost_or_limit: The passage gives no schedule beyond saying it opened again.
forgotten-realms.rule.wildtide-arrivals.go_wrong: Arrivals can be attacked on entry.
forgotten-realms.rule.wildtide-arrivals.where_from: Serôs and the Sea of Corynactis.
forgotten-realms.rule.wildtide-arrivals.combines: The portal enabled two separate waves of migration.

forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.name: magical controls over aranea

effect.summary: Tulan's magical controls made aranea effective soldiers.

forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.cost_or_limit: The passage gives no control range, duration, or resistance.
forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.mind: The controls imply influence but no mental effect is detailed.
forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.who_may: Tulan el Akada controlled the aranea.
forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.combines: Used in the war against drow.
forgotten-realms.rule.magical-controls-o.blocked_reason: The passage does not specify how control is imposed or resisted.

forgotten-realms.rule.female-heir-regenc.name: female heir regency

effect.summary: If no male heir is old enough, a suitable female heir rules until one comes of age; the ruler is called emperor regardless of sex.

forgotten-realms.rule.female-heir-regenc.cost_or_limit: Applies when male heirs are not of age.

forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.name: wan shades reclaim identities

effect.summary: Shadows freed from their masters can recover their identities and seek their pasts.

forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.go_wrong: Some are destroyed before recovering their pasts.
forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.combines: Their former master’s destruction frees them
forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.blocked_reason: Restoring identity and personal history to undead requires soul and memory-state mechanics.

forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.name: Dark Fissure planar rift

effect.summary: Portals to the Abyss open a massive rift that pulls constructs into otherness.

forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.cost_or_limit: Requires the drithdarkar to open portals.
forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.go_wrong: The rift removes the advancing constructs from the battlefield.
forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.blocked_reason: A large-scale rift affects an army over an area.

forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.name: Ninety-nine years of service for Eltab’s release

effect.summary: Myrkul’s followers agree to serve Eltab for ninety-nine years in return for releasing him.

forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.go_wrong: The bargain frees Eltab and enables his rise to power.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.who_may: The followers of Myrkul make the agreement.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.combines: Exchanges service for release from binding.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.blocked_reason: It requires a binding and release condition with a duration and exchange.

forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.name: Laws of Battle

effect.summary: Rules drafted to prevent a recurrence of genocidal slaughter like the battles against the merrow.

forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.cost_or_limit: Intended to constrain warfare and prevent mass slaughter.
forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.who_may: Drafted by merfolk, shalarins, and Dukars
forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.blocked_reason: The passage gives their purpose but no specific unsupported game effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.name: Myth Nantar's expanding mythal

effect.summary: Where the mythal reaches, it bars matter and magic except corals, sea stars, and fish.

forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.cost_or_limit: Its protection spreads gradually over the city.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.go_wrong: Touching it produces haunting singing and discourages nearby visitors.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.mind: The singing influences local beliefs about a curse.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.where_from: The mythal surrounding the Academy of the Dukars.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.combines: Exempts corals, sea stars, and fish.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.blocked_reason: Its gradual, area-wide selective barrier is more than a simple instantaneous block.

forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.name: Sacred Secrets

effect.summary: The location of the replaying door is kept secret by Azuth and Mystra.

forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.cost_or_limit: Access to the location is limited to the secret's holders.
forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.who_may: Azuth and Mystra share the secret.
forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.blocked_reason: The rule concerns concealment of information.

forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.name: Wulgreth's transformation into a lich

effect.summary: Unleashed magical energies transform Wulgreth into a lich.

forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.cost_or_limit: Occurs upon his death amid released magical energies.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.go_wrong: The event creates the Dire Wood as well.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.where_from: Magical energies released when he dies.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.blocked_reason: Changing a being into a lich is a substantial form transformation.

forgotten-realms.rule.wisdom-and-not-arm.name: wisdom and not armed might will rule in the city

effect.summary: Waterdeep’s rule is to rest on wisdom rather than military force.

forgotten-realms.rule.wisdom-and-not-arm.blocked_reason: This is a governance rule rather than a special game effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.name: Magic bowls’ duration and poison limitation

effect.summary: The bowls' clear-thought benefit lasts an hour and does not prevent poisoning.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.cost_or_limit: One hour of benefit; no poison protection
forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.blocked_reason: The duration and stated limitation can be tracked with ordinary effect duration and item rules.

forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.name: Enchanted collar distance restriction

effect.summary: The wearer cannot move farther than a set distance from the Master.

forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.cost_or_limit: Movement is limited by an unspecified radius
forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.blocked_reason: The restriction acts continuously on a bound person.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.name: The Time of Troubles

effect.summary: Gods are forced to walk the Realms as mortals while magic grows unreliable and prayers fail.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.cost_or_limit: The gods seek the Tablets of Fate to return to their domains
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.go_wrong: Magic becomes unpredictable and divine prayers go unanswered
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.where_from: Lord Ao casts the gods out of their domains
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.combines: The Tablets of Fate are the key to the gods’ return
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.blocked_reason: The rule involves divine embodiment and return between planes, beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.name: Godstrife’s awakening of Myth Rhynn

effect.summary: An awakening of evil in the ruins imbues nearby creatures with a drive to maraud together.

forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.go_wrong: Disparate creatures are compelled to act together despite their usual hostility
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.mind: Imposes a desire to maraud and despoil
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.combines: The creatures move in bands despite differing natures
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.blocked_reason: The rule imposes a lasting drive on creatures’ minds.

forgotten-realms.rule.death-and-rebirth-.name: Death and rebirth of Torm

effect.summary: Torm dies and is later reborn during the Time of Troubles.

forgotten-realms.rule.death-and-rebirth-.blocked_reason: Death and subsequent divine rebirth require a soul-state mechanic.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.name: The Shaking Plague

effect.summary: A contagious illness causes pallor and uncontrollable shaking; some recover after months, while severe cases die.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.cost_or_limit: Contagious for roughly ten days after onset; prior victims become less susceptible.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.go_wrong: Severe spasms can prevent breathing and cause death.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.blocked_reason: The passage provides a gameable disease process and duration.

forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.name: Life-extending magic in the red gem

effect.summary: Akhlaur and Zalathorm owe their long lives to magic they made together; destroying its final gem-held portion kills them.

forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.cost_or_limit: The remaining power is housed in the gem.
forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.go_wrong: Destroying the gem ends their lives.
forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.blocked_reason: The passage establishes a power-bearing item and lethal loss but gives no operating or depletion rules.

forgotten-realms.rule.demons-beneath-dun.name: Demons beneath Dun-Tharos awaken

effect.summary: The struggle stirs previously dormant demons beneath the ruins.

forgotten-realms.rule.demons-beneath-dun.cost_or_limit: The struggle is the stated catalyst.

forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.name: Rage of Dragons ends

effect.summary: Ending the High Magic that caused the dragon rage ends the Rage.

forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.cost_or_limit: The rage is sustained by elven High Magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.go_wrong: Dragons were driven into a widespread rage.
forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.combines: Its end releases Bahamut from an ancient prison.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.name: Dead raised as shadows

effect.summary: Volumvax raises the dead of Ordulin as shadows to strengthen his army.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.cost_or_limit: Requires Volumvax’s action; other limits are unstated.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.go_wrong: The dead become hostile army members.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.mind: Their new allegiance is not explained.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.blocked_reason: The transformation and continued state of the dead are not runnable with the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.name: Kiaransalee erased from the Realms

effect.summary: With her name and worshipers removed, the deity fades from existence.

forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.cost_or_limit: The account links the erasure to High Magic and loss of worshipers.
forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.who_may: Q’arlynd Melarn and apprentices perform the ritual.
forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.blocked_reason: The disappearance and cessation of a deity’s existence require a soul-state mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.name: Elven High Magic causes dragon rage

effect.summary: A High Magic working causes dragons to enter a rage.

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.cost_or_limit: The rage lasts until the working ends.
forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.combines: Ending the working ends the rage.
forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.blocked_reason: It affects dragons broadly across a region rather than a single target.
